Looking at again after a period of months, I think I can pull out the fact that :

on a finite-dimensional real normed space, a continuous bilinear form ϕ\phiϕ that is symmetric and positive-definite induces a norm v↦(φ v v)v \mapsto \sqrt{(φ\, v\, v)}v↦(φvv)​, and that norm generates the same topology as the given norm and so the open unit ball {v ∣ ϕ v v<1}\{v \,|\, \phi\, v\, v < 1\}{v∣ϕvv<1} is von Neumann bounded.

Of course it means generalising and extracting what I have written and it now has nothing to do with manifolds. It may even be helpful for creating a Riemannian metric on the n-sphere

I am getting a lot of negative vibes here but anyway the split (thank you @Kevin Buzzard for the prompt) was easier than I imagined and I now have a 300 LoC result:

For a positive-definite symmetric continuous bilinear form φ on a finite-dimensional real normed space, the set {v | φ v v < 1} is von Neumann bounded.

And then a 400 LoC result:

Riemannian metrics exist.

I will modify the existing PR to start with and then create two PRs: one for each result.

I am not convinced that you are doing it in the right generality: why only do it in finite dimension? Everything should be fine if the fiber of your vector bundle (which is a normed space) admits an equivalent norm given by an inner product. Also, I see that your file starts with

variable {B : Type*}
  {E : B → Type*}
  [∀ x, NormedAddCommGroup (E x)]

section tangentSpaceEquiv

variable [∀ x, NormedSpace ℝ (E x)]

The word tangentSpaceEquiv seems to imply that you will only work on tangent spaces, but the variables rather seem to indicate a general vector bundle. Also, you are assuming from the start a normed space structure on your fibers, which is really strange since you should only need topological vector spaces.

To me, all these are signs indicate that your PR seems far from being ready for Mathlib. This might explain why you are not getting any feedback here.

That is useful. I have removed the normed space structure on the fibers. The theorem is proved for general vector bundles; there is no mention now of tangents.

I think a theorem that says every finite dimensional manifold possesses a Riemannian metric is valuable in its own right. If at some point, someone produces a more general proof then this theorem could either be deprecated or given a very simple proof.

Maybe we are hamstrung by this at the moment:

SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate.{uι, uE, uH, uM} {ι : Type uι} {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) {M : Type uM} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [IsManifold I ∞ M] [T2Space M] [SigmaCompactSpace M] {s : Set M}
  (hs : IsClosed s) (U : ι → Set M) (ho : ∀ (i : ι), IsOpen (U i)) (hU : s ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) : ∃ f, f.IsSubordinate U
On the other hand, weakening [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] to [CompleteSpace F] looks feasible but as a strategy, how about landing this first and then making that generalisation?

how about landing this first and then making that generalisation

Usually, that's not how mathlib proceeds. If the proof doesn't need significant changes, I'd prefer the generalized version to land.

SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate

Mathematically, the existence of smooth partitions of unity is somewhat subtle. I'm not sure if Hausdorffness is import here; I'll assume it for simplicity of discussion.

  • Every second countable Hausdorff Banach manifold possesses a continuous partition of unity (and perhaps you don't need being Banach Banach).
  • Every second countable Hausdorff Hilbert manifold possesses a smooth partition of unity.
  • For general Banach manifolds, this is rather subtle. I went into that rabbit hole once... if you want to construct a smooth partition of unity on your Banach manifold, in general you may be asking the wrong question.

So, I am quite sure your lemma should generalise to any-dimensional Hilbert manifolds. I am not convinced it will generalise to any Banach manifold (what you're proposing above). In the long term, a class HasSmoothPartitionOfUnity might be the way to go; I don't think that has to happen in your PR.

The current SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate assumes [FiniteDimensional ℝ E], and generalising to Hilbert manifolds would need a more general version of it. There's also [SigmaCompactSpace M] to worry about since infinite-dimensional manifolds aren't locally compact. And as you noted, it can't be fully general as there are Banach spaces with no smooth bump functions, hence Banach manifolds with no smooth partitions of unity.

I think weakening [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] to [CompleteSpace F] would require significant changes which is why I am suggesting landing the finite dimensional version first.

There are two different finite-dimensionality assumptions here: for the base manifold, and for the fiber. For the base manifold, finite-dimensionality is very natural (that's what makes partitions of unity possible), and I don't think we should change it. For the fiber, there is absolutely no reason to assume finite-dimensionality: just assume that your fiber is an inner product space, or isomorphic to an inner product space.
